_note: The intake engine's settings (docs/INGEST.md). Everything that comes in (a video, a screenshot, a web page, a Showdown paste, a research result) becomes a card of proposed claims; nothing reaches canon until it's approved. The analyzer writes the same envelope Food OS writes (source, analysis, result with summary, transcript, on-screen text, observations, limitations), plus one block per lens, so a shared intake engine for every project can take this over later.

gemini._note: Video, image and page analysis runs on Google's Gemini API, the same provider and model family Food OS uses. The key is read from the environment variable below (set it in the cloud environment's settings, never in chat or in a file). The API bills per token; Food OS's results record about 7,500 to 14,000 tokens per video.
gemini._models_note: Answers stream back (streamGenerateContent), so a long analysis isn't cut off by the network proxy's 30-second limit on a silent request. When the model is busy (503) or rate-limited (429), it waits and retries, then tries the fallbacks in order.

download._note: A link's title and creator come from the site's oEmbed endpoint when it has one (platforms.*.oembed), else from yt-dlp. TikTok, Instagram and other links are downloaded with yt-dlp, then uploaded to Gemini. YouTube links go to Gemini directly (no download). Each site's domain must be allowed in the environment's network settings.

review._note: Who approves. Everything goes through you by default. List a provenance here (e.g. 'cartridge') to let its claims approve themselves; leave it empty to see everything.

claims._note: What a claim can be, and where an approved one lands. 'requires' lists the fields a claim must have before it can be approved (a build needs its generation; nothing external is trusted without a source).

field_note.label: species field note (behavior, habitat, diet, social life)

build.label: a build (yours, or external with its source)

lore.label: a canon fact (show, games, manga), with its citation

trainer_version.label: a new version of a trainer, with its roster (anime, manga, all-time, custom; never overwrites one)

style_card.label: a video's style, for the documentary prompt kit

correction.label: a correction to something already in canon

corrections._note: Which canon values a correction may change, as file + path patterns. Anything else is refused.
corrections._versions: A correction to a build (canon/build_library.json) makes a new version of it: the old values are kept under the build's history with their version number, so nothing is overwritten (MASTER_PLAN §4.2). A trainer's roster changes by a new version (trainer_version with parent), never in place.

lenses._note: A lens is what the analyzer is asked to look for. The core (summary, transcript, on-screen text, observations, limitations) is the same for every lens; the block is the lens's own.

pokemon.prompt:
You are watching material for a Pokémon research archive (games, anime, manga, fan documentaries). Report only what the material shows or says, with a timestamp (mm:ss) for every item; never fill gaps from memory. Return one JSON object with exactly these keys:

summary: two sentences on what this is.
transcript: [{timestamp, text}] every spoken line, in order (narration and dialogue), in the original language with an English translation in brackets if it isn't English.
on_screen_text: [{timestamp, text}] captions, titles, menus, battle text.
observations: [{timestamp, text}] what is visible, shot by shot, in plain words.
limitations: [text] what the material doesn't show or can't settle.
pokemon: {
  videoType: one of NATURE_DOCUMENTARY, ANIME_CLIP, GAMEPLAY, BATTLE, TEAMBUILDING, EXPLAINER, FAN_ANIMATION, OTHER,
  species: [{name, evidence: [{from: speech|onscreen|visual|caption, text, at}], confidence: HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW}],
  behaviors: [{species, behavior, context, at}]  (feeding, hunting, nesting, play, social, migration, defense, battle style),
  habitats: [{species, habitat, time_of_day, weather, season, region_if_named, at}],
  battle: [{trainer, pokemon, move, situation, outcome, at}]  (who used what, when, and what happened; situation is even, ahead or behind if you can tell),
  builds: [{species, nickname, moves, item, ability, nature, evs, ivs, level, game_or_generation, at}]  (only when a set is shown or stated),
  lore: [{subject, fact, episode_or_title, at}]  (canon facts the material states),
  style: {narration_voice, narrator_perspective, pacing, music, tone, color_and_light, structure: [beats in order], shots: [{at, shot, framing, camera_move, subject}]},
  creatorClaims: [text]  (opinions or claims the creator makes that the material doesn't prove),
  notInVideo: [text]  (things a researcher would want that this doesn't show)
}
Use empty lists for anything absent. Names: official English Pokémon names.
pokemon.fan_note: From a fan work: its interpretation, not canon. Approve it as canon only if you want it in your world.

doc_prompt._note: The documentary prompt kit: a narration brief and shot-by-shot prompts for a video tool (Sora, Veo, Runway…), grounded in approved field notes and an approved style card. Edit the templates freely.
doc_prompt.narration: Write narration in the voice of {narration_voice}, {narrator_perspective}. Tone: {tone}. Pacing: {pacing}. Shape it like this (the shape only; every event in it comes from the field notes): {structure}. The subject is {species} in {setting}. Everything the narration says about {species} must come from these field notes, nothing invented: {notes}. Length: about {seconds} seconds read aloud.
doc_prompt.shot: {framing} of {subject} ({species}) in {setting}, {camera_move}. {color_and_light}. Nature documentary realism, no on-screen text. Behavior: {behavior}.

bulbapedia._note: Bulbapedia research (ingest/bulbapedia.py): the ASK list answered from the page source. Text is CC BY-NC-SA 2.5 (fine for a personal, non-commercial project): every claim cites its page, and pages are cached in data/raw/bulbapedia (never committed).
bulbapedia.license: Bulbapedia text, CC BY-NC-SA 2.5: cited per claim
bulbapedia._aniseries_note: How a page names each series in its History headings: the {{aniseries}} code (Pokémon pages use AG for Advanced Generation, character pages RS) or the series title.

GS: Pokémon the Series: Gold and Silver
AG: Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire
DP: Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl

bulbapedia._eras_note: Each anime version's era: the episodes its moves-used rows may come from, the History stretch it reads, and the moment the version stands for (what the model is asked about).

ash/kanto.moment: the Indigo Plateau Conference at the end of the Indigo League

ash/sinnoh.moment: the Lily of the Valley Conference

paul/sinnoh.moment: Paul's full battle against Ash at the Lily of the Valley Conference

gary/johto.moment: Gary's full battle against Ash at the Silver Conference

bulbapedia._battles_note: The battle each rival version is remembered for, and how to find the order its Pokémon came out in: sentences on the Pokémon's page (its era's history) or the trainer page entry that give an ordinal ('the fifth Pokémon used'), name one of the words and the opponent. The words must name that battle alone ('Full Battle' also matches Ash and Paul's earlier one at Lake Acuity).

paul/sinnoh.label: the Lily of the Valley Conference full battle against Ash

ash/sinnoh.label: the Lily of the Valley Conference full battle against Paul

gary/johto.label: the Silver Conference full battle against Ash

bulbapedia._late_note: Without the model, the moveset at a version's moment is read from the last part of the era's history (this share of it): the moves named closest to the era's end, then the most named.

signature._note: A signature move is confirmed when the era's history names it among the top this many of its moves.

pokedex._note: The Pokédex cross-check (ingest/pokedex.py): a field note or lore claim is backed by a game's Pokédex entry when they share at least shared_at_least content words (after folding the synonyms below) and the overlap (shared / the shorter's words) reaches backs_at. Backing is evidence for review, never an approval.
